subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an A.P.
stem: If the first term of an A.P. is \(p\), the second term is \(q\) and the last term is \(r\), then show that the sum of all the terms is \((q + r - 2p) \times \dfrac{(p + r)}{2(q - p)}\).
solution:
The common difference \(d = q - p\). Let there be \(n\) terms with last term \(r\).
\(r = p + (n - 1)d \Rightarrow n - 1 = \dfrac{r - p}{q - p} \Rightarrow n = \dfrac{r - p}{q - p} + 1 = \dfrac{r - p + q - p}{q - p} = \dfrac{q + r - 2p}{q - p}\).
Sum \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(\text{first term} + \text{last term}) = \dfrac{n}{2}(p + r) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{q + r - 2p}{q - p} \cdot (p + r) = (q + r - 2p) \times \dfrac{(p + r)}{2(q - p)}\). Hence proved.

stem:
Show the following data by a frequency polygon:

| Electricity bill (₹) | Families |
|---|---|
| 200–400 | 240 |
| 400–600 | 300 |
| 600–800 | 450 |
| 800–1000 | 350 |
| 1000–1200 | 160 |
solution:
Find the class mark (mid-value) of each class and plot the point (class mark, frequency); join them by line segments, with the two ends brought down to the mid-values of the imagined adjacent classes (frequency 0).
Class marks and frequencies: \((300, 240)\), \((500, 300)\), \((700, 450)\), \((900, 350)\), \((1100, 160)\); with the end points \((100, 0)\) at the start and \((1300, 0)\) at the end. Plotting these seven points and joining them in order gives the required frequency polygon.

stem: The sum of the squares of five consecutive natural numbers is 1455. Find the numbers.
solution:
Let the five consecutive natural numbers be \(n-2, n-1, n, n+1, n+2\).
Sum of squares \(= (n-2)^2 + (n-1)^2 + n^2 + (n+1)^2 + (n+2)^2 = 5n^2 + 10 = 1455\).
\(5n^2 = 1445 \Rightarrow n^2 = 289 \Rightarrow n = 17\) (natural number).
\(\therefore\) the numbers are \(15, 16, 17, 18, 19\). (Check: \(225 + 256 + 289 + 324 + 361 = 1455\).)
